2027-05-08.title: Sixth Saturday of Resurrection
2027-05-08.readTitle: Readings of the day (First Set; mapped from the official calendar, verify locally)
readings: He will baptize you with the Holy Spirit and fire
2027-05-08.alt: Season of the Resurrection (Qyamta), in the days between the Ascension and Pentecost. The Holy Qurbana is celebrated with the Anaphora of Addai and Mari, and the Queen of Heaven (Regina Caeli) is prayed in place of the Angelus until Pentecost. The second day of the novena to the Holy Spirit; a Saturday in the Marian month of May.
2027-05-08.verse: I baptize you with water for repentance, but one who is more powerful than I is coming after me; I am not worthy to carry his sandals. He will baptize you with the Holy Spirit and fire.
theo: Between the Ascension and Pentecost the Church takes us back to the banks of the Jordan, to the first promise of the Spirit in the Gospel. John the Baptist sees many Pharisees and Sadducees coming for baptism, and he speaks with the bluntness of a prophet: “Bear fruit worthy of repentance.” He is not condemning a whole people; he is speaking to religious leaders of his own nation, as the prophets of Israel always did, and his words strike every religious person in every age, ourselves first. He warns them against a comfortable security: “Do not presume to say to yourselves, ‘We have Abraham as our ancestor’; for I tell you, God is able from these stones to raise up children to Abraham.” A Christian can say the same kind of thing: I was baptised as a child, my family has been Catholic since the time of St Thomas, our parish is ancient. All true, and all precious. But none of it replaces the fruit of a converted life. “Even now the ax is lying at the root of the trees.” The time is short, and God looks for fruit, not for family trees.

Then John points away from himself: “I baptize you with water for repentance, but one who is more powerful than I is coming after me; I am not worthy to carry his sandals. He will baptize you with the Holy Spirit and fire.” Water washes; fire transforms. John's baptism prepared the heart; the baptism of Jesus gives the Spirit himself. That promise is fulfilled at Pentecost, when “divided tongues, as of fire, appeared among them, and a tongue rested on each of them. All of them were filled with the Holy Spirit” (Acts 2:3–4). In these nine days we pray for that fire. It is not a fire that destroys the person; it burns away the chaff and leaves the wheat. “His winnowing fork is in his hand, and he will clear his threshing floor and will gather his wheat into the granary.” A Kerala farmer who has seen paddy winnowed in the wind knows the picture: the light husk flies away, the heavy grain falls at his feet. The Spirit does in us what the wind does on the threshing floor. What is empty in us is blown away; what is good is gathered into God's granary.

Paul speaks to the Corinthians about another kind of fruit: a heart given entirely to the Lord. “The unmarried man is anxious about the affairs of the Lord, how to please the Lord; but the married man is anxious about the affairs of the world, how to please his wife, and his interests are divided.” Paul is not despising marriage; in the same letter he calls marriage a gift from God (1 Corinthians 7:7), and the Church honours it as a sacrament. He is speaking of a particular call, celibacy for the sake of the kingdom, which lets a person belong to the Lord with an undivided heart. His purpose is clear: “I say this for your own benefit, not to put any restraint upon you, but to promote good order and unhindered devotion to the Lord.” Every Christian, married or not, is called to that undivided devotion in his or her own state of life. On this Saturday of May we look to the Virgin Mary, whose heart was never divided: she belonged wholly to God, and she was also the most devoted of mothers. In the upper room she prayed with the apostles for the Spirit who had come upon her at Nazareth (Luke 1:35). Let us ask her to obtain for us, in this novena, the fire that makes the heart whole.
conn: The Spirit and fire at Pentecost.
“Divided tongues, as of fire, appeared among them, and a tongue rested on each of them. All of them were filled with the Holy Spirit” (Acts 2:3–4).
“For he is like a refiner's fire and like fullers' soap” (Malachi 3:2): the Lord purifies his people as gold is purified.
Paul writes, “if you belong to Christ, then you are Abraham's offspring, heirs according to the promise” (Galatians 3:29).
Jesus repeats John's warning: “Every tree that does not bear good fruit is cut down and thrown into the fire. Thus you will know them by their fruits” (Matthew 7:19–20).
“The Holy Spirit will come upon you, and the power of the Most High will overshadow you” (Luke 1:35).
Jesus speaks of those who renounce marriage “for the sake of the kingdom of heaven” (Matthew 19:12).
altar: At the Holy Qurbana the priest calls down the Holy Spirit in the epiclesis, that he may come and dwell on the offering. The fire John promised comes to rest on the bread and wine, and through them on us.

Those who serve the altar with an undivided heart, priests and religious, are a gift to the Church. Pray for them at this Qurbana, and offer your own heart, in whatever state of life, without division.
outline: From the Ascension back to the Jordan: the first promise of the Spirit.
Point 1 · Bear fruit worthy of repentance
Family trees are precious, but God looks for fruit.
Point 2 · The Holy Spirit and fire
Water washes, fire transforms; the winnowing of the heart.
Point 3 · Unhindered devotion to the Lord
Celibacy for the kingdom, the holiness of marriage, and the undivided heart of Mary.
Paddy winnowed in the wind on a threshing floor in Kuttanad.
“He will baptize you with the Holy Spirit and fire.”
live: Choose one concrete fruit of conversion for this week: a reconciliation, an apology, an honest account.
In the novena today, ask the Holy Spirit to burn away one habit that is only chaff in your life.
Give the Lord one hour this weekend with nothing else in your hands: no phone, no work, only prayer.
Pray a decade of the rosary today with Mary for priests, religious and families, that their hearts may be undivided.
fathers: The Lord baptizes with the Holy Spirit and fire because the grace of the Spirit is like fire: it burns away the thorns of sin and makes the soul shine, as iron placed in the fire takes on its glow. What fire does to iron, the Spirit does to the soul that receives him.

Let the life of the Virgin Mary be set before you like a picture, in which, as in a mirror, the beauty of chastity and the form of every virtue shine. From her we learn what to correct, what to imitate and what to hold fast.
magis: Fire symbolizes the transforming energy of the Holy Spirit's actions. John the Baptist proclaims Christ as the one who will baptize with the Holy Spirit and with fire; in the form of tongues as of fire the Spirit rests on the disciples at Pentecost.
Jesus calls to conversion. This call is addressed first to those who do not yet know Christ, and also to Christians, for whom conversion is an uninterrupted task for the whole Church.

Christ is the centre of all Christian life. Virginity for the sake of the kingdom of heaven is an unfolding of baptismal grace; both the sacrament of Matrimony and virginity for the kingdom come from the Lord himself, and they reinforce each other.
Mary is a virgin because her virginity is the sign of her faith unadulterated by any doubt, and of her undivided gift of herself to God's will.
saints: 7–13 May: the days after the Ascension of our Lord (Thursday 6 May), when the apostles waited in prayer for the Holy Spirit “together with certain women, including Mary the mother of Jesus” (Acts 1:14). Many families and parishes pray a novena to the Holy Spirit from Friday 7 to Saturday 15 May, the eve of Pentecost. Fri 7: First Friday. Sun 9: Seventh Sunday of Resurrection, the Sunday after the Ascension; the Latin Church in India celebrates the Ascension on this Sunday. Mon 10: in the Latin calendar, St John of Avila. Wed 12: in the Latin calendar, Sts Nereus and Achilleus and St Pancras. Thu 13: in the Latin calendar, Our Lady of Fatima. The Marian month of May continues (verify locally).
2027-05-08.prayer: Lord Jesus Christ, more powerful than John, you baptize with the Holy Spirit and fire. In these days of waiting, burn away the chaff in our hearts and gather the wheat into your granary. Keep us from trusting in our name or our history; make us bear fruit worthy of repentance. Give to your priests and religious undivided hearts, and to our families a devotion to you that nothing can divide. Through the prayers of the Virgin Mary, whose heart was wholly yours, send us your Spirit at Pentecost. Amen. Alleluia!

quick: John the Baptist: bear fruit worthy of repentance; God looks for fruit, not family trees.
He will baptize you with the Holy Spirit and fire: the promise fulfilled at Pentecost.
Paul: an undivided heart and unhindered devotion to the Lord.
2027-05-08.action: Choose one concrete fruit of conversion for this week, and pray the novena with Mary today.
2027-05-08.question: What chaff in my life do I need the fire of the Spirit to blow away?
kidsaint: Rose Eluvathingal was born in 1877 at Kattoor near Thrissur. As a girl she wanted to belong only to Jesus, and she became a sister of the Congregation of the Mother of Carmel, taking the name Euphrasia. At the convent in Ollur she prayed so much that people called her the ‘praying mother’. She died in 1952, and Pope Francis declared her a saint in 2014. Lesson: a heart that belongs to Jesus has room for everyone who needs prayer.
2027-05-08.special: Sixth Saturday of Resurrection. A Saturday of the Marian month of May; second day of the novena to the Holy Spirit.
term: The old way of separating grain from husk: the threshed crop is tossed into the wind with a winnowing fork or a flat basket, so that the light chaff blows away and the heavy grain falls. John the Baptist uses the picture for the judgment of the Messiah, and the Church sees in it the work of the Holy Spirit, who separates what is empty from what is good.

family.explain: John the Baptist baptized people in the river Jordan with water. But he said: someone greater is coming, and he will baptize you with the Holy Spirit and fire! Fire gives light and warmth, and it makes things clean. At Pentecost the Holy Spirit came on the disciples like little flames of fire. The Holy Spirit wants to make our hearts warm with love and bright with goodness.
family.intention: We pray for priests and sisters, who give their whole heart to Jesus, and for all families.
family.ask: Ask: “What is one good fruit our family can give God this week?”

illus: An old farmer in Kuttanad used to winnow the paddy by hand long after machines came to the village. His grandson once asked why he waited for the evening wind instead of finishing in the morning. The old man lifted a basket of grain, let it fall slowly, and the husk flew away over the bund while the grain dropped at his feet. ‘The wind knows what is heavy and what is empty,’ he said. ‘I only have to lift it up.’ In these days before Pentecost we lift up our hearts to the Wind of God. What is empty in us he blows away; what is good he gathers.

pm.open: Holy Spirit, fire of God, come upon us as we gather. With Mary, who prayed with the apostles for your coming, we open our hearts to you. Amen. Alleluia!
share: Bear fruit worthy of repentance (Matthew 3:8). What fruit is the Lord looking for in my life now?
Do not presume to say to yourselves, ‘We have Abraham as our ancestor’ (Matthew 3:9). On what do I rely instead of real conversion?
He will baptize you with the Holy Spirit and fire (Matthew 3:11). What would I like the Spirit's fire to change in me?
Unhindered devotion to the Lord (1 Corinthians 7:35). What divides my heart?
pm.resp: Come, Holy Spirit, kindle in us the fire of your love.
interc: For the Church, that she may be renewed by the fire of the Spirit at Pentecost.
For priests and religious, that they may serve with undivided hearts.
For married couples, that their love may be holy and faithful.
For young people discerning their call, that they may hear the Lord and answer generously.
For all who rely on their past instead of turning to God today, that they may bear fruit.
pm.close: Father, your Son promised to baptize us with the Holy Spirit and fire. Through the prayers of the Virgin Mary, send your Spirit to make our hearts whole and our lives fruitful, through Christ our Lord. Amen. Alleluia!

homily: Dear friends, today the Gospel takes us to the river Jordan, where John the Baptist is preaching. Many religious leaders come to him, and he tells them: “Bear fruit worthy of repentance.”

He warns them not to say, ‘We have Abraham as our father.’ We can say similar things: I was baptised as a baby, my family is old Catholic, my parish is ancient. Thank God for all that! But God looks for fruit. What fruit is in my life today?

Then John says: one more powerful than I is coming; “He will baptize you with the Holy Spirit and fire.” This promise came true at Pentecost, when tongues of fire rested on the disciples. In these nine days we pray for that fire. It does not destroy us; it burns away the chaff and keeps the wheat, as the wind does on the threshing floor.

Paul speaks of an undivided heart. Some are called to give themselves wholly to the Lord in priesthood or religious life. Others are called to marriage, which is also holy. Every one of us is called to “unhindered devotion to the Lord” in our own state of life.

On this Saturday of May let us look to Mary. Her heart was never divided; she belonged wholly to God, and she was a loving mother. She prayed with the apostles for the Spirit. Let us ask her today: Mother, pray with us, that the fire of the Spirit may come on us at Pentecost. Alleluia! Amen.
kids: Children, John the Baptist said that Jesus would give us the Holy Spirit and fire. Fire gives light and warmth.
When the Holy Spirit comes into your heart, he makes it warm with love and bright with goodness. Ask him today: ‘Holy Spirit, make my heart warm and bright!’

intro: Theme: “He will baptize you with the Holy Spirit and fire.”
The second day of the novena: fruit worthy of repentance, the fire that winnows the heart, and the undivided devotion of which Mary is the model.

sub: A prophet speaking to his own people.
q: Cast away from you all the transgressions that you have committed against me, and get yourselves a new heart and a new spirit! Why will you die, O house of Israel?
points.apply: Choose one concrete fruit of conversion this week and do it before Pentecost.

q: But who can endure the day of his coming, and who can stand when he appears? For he is like a refiner's fire and like fullers' soap.
He will baptize you with the Holy Spirit and fire.
points.apply: In the novena each day, ask the Spirit to burn away one habit that is only chaff.

q: Teach me your way, O LORD, that I may walk in your truth; give me an undivided heart to revere your name.
I say this for your own benefit, not to put any restraint upon you, but to promote good order and unhindered devotion to the Lord.
points.apply: Give the Lord one undivided hour this weekend, and pray with Mary for vocations and families.

concl: God looks for fruit, and the Spirit's fire makes the heart whole.
With Mary, let us pray for that fire in these days of waiting.
2027-05-08.resolve: This week, bear one fruit of conversion, give the Lord an undivided hour, and pray the novena daily with Mary.
